title: New Horizons for the Methodology and Physiology of Training Periodization
claims: Traditional training periodization was established in the 1960s and divides the seasonal programme into smaller periods and training units.

The review lists limitations of traditional periodization: conflicting physiological responses from mixed training directed at many abilities, excessive fatigue from prolonged multi-targeted training, insufficient stimulation from medium- and low-concentration workloads, and inability to provide multi-peak performances over the season.
Block periodization sequences specialized training cycles (blocks) that contain highly concentrated workloads directed at a minimal number of targeted abilities.
Unlike the traditional model's simultaneous development of many abilities, block-periodized training presupposes consecutive development of selected target abilities.
The block model is set out through general principles, a taxonomy of mesocycle blocks, and guidelines for compiling an annual plan.
